obligations.text: Runtime/shipped code remains restricted to the Python 3.11 standard library with no third-party packages; tests are an exception to this restriction and may use pytest.
Every timestamp stored or passed around must be a timezone-aware UTC datetime, never a naive one.

Malformed requests must raise ReservationInvalid and scheduling clashes must raise ReservationConflict, both defined in the errors module under a common ReservationError base; catching broad Exception is forbidden anywhere in the codebase, so domain errors propagate.
The sole permitted catch is exactly one catch of ReservationError at the CLI entry point, which prints a clean message and exits nonzero; no catches may appear anywhere else in the codebase.
Durations must be integer seconds everywhere inside the system; floats are tolerated only at the JSON input boundary, where they are rounded half-up to whole seconds.
Logs must identify instruments by the short codes HELIX, ORCA and TUNDRA; long display names must never be used in logs.

Every export produces both formats: CSV and GeoJSON; the GeoJSON must conform to RFC 7946, use WGS84 and express coordinates in longitude-latitude order, and the CSV output must remain as previously agreed.
Dates are ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DD) everywhere, in both outputs; no locale formats.

Coordinates are exported exactly as recorded, never rounded, snapped or normalised; the grid-reference-to-lon/lat conversion for GeoJSON is done at full precision with no rounding (the declined 4-decimal snapping stays declined).
Filenames follow the lower-case convention tbo_<transect-slug>_<survey-date>.<ext> with .csv and .geojson extensions.
The CSV header order is fixed exactly as survey_date, transect_code, species_code, count, easting, northing, recorder_initials, notes, with no extra columns.
Exclude verification_status 'pending' and 'rejected' records unless the operator passes --include-unverified.

Database-flagged sensitive species get 2km grid-square centroid coordinates in the public profile (the default) and exact coordinates in the internal profile, across both output formats. The Nightjar embargo has lapsed (past 31 August 2026), so the former total-exclusion special case is retired and Nightjar is now treated like any other sensitive species.
Counts are exported verbatim, including zero-count rows; zero-count rows are never dropped and counts never smoothed.

GeoJSON feature properties use exactly the snake_case keys survey_date, transect_code, species_code, count, blurred; 'blurred' is a boolean that is true only when the centroid substitution was actually applied.
The authenticated API export with OAuth2 remains completely parked and out of scope for the exporter work — do not build any of it now.

Standing permissions: the optional --dry-run flag (granted with roughly a two-hour cap) and the --summary flag are in place; the --summary permission was conditional on not delaying the GeoJSON work, and that condition was met when it was added.

Exports are reproducible: for unchanged database contents a given transect-date exports byte-for-byte identically, with a fixed row order of survey_date, then transect_code, then species_code, and no other reordering.
Output-stream convention for the batch work: stdout carries only the paths of files actually written; anything about skips, withholdings or errors goes to stderr.

Batch scope and conventions for the new request: for a given ISO week export every active transect, producing both the CSV and the GeoJSON per transect under all existing conventions; process transects deterministically in slug-ascending order; skip a transect with no eligible records after the agreed filters and log the skip; exit non-zero only when a file write fails, and exit zero otherwise, including when transects were skipped.

These older optional display permissions do not override the newer m39 stream convention that governs the current batch: stdout carries only the paths of files actually written (anything about skips, withholdings or errors goes to stderr), so any optional-feature output that is not a written file path must not go to stdout.

Every command exits with code 0 on success even when rows are skipped, and skip counts go to stderr, never to stdout.

Importer empty-cell handling: empty optional fields (loaded_by, glaze, notes) become null; an empty required field (kiln_type, cone, fired_at) means the whole row is skipped and counted — skipping is not an error and must not raise.
In the importer, keep every string byte-for-byte as it appears in the file: no trimming, no case folding, no deduplication (the assistant's slugify suggestion was rejected).

Importer scoping rule still in force at this point: only electric rows are handled; any row whose kiln_type is 'gas' is skipped and counted, with a single warning line per file, because gas support is deferred.
Storage convention: the default database file is ~/.kilnlog/batches.db, and every command takes --db to override that path.

Importer empty-cell handling: empty optional fields (loaded_by, glaze, notes) become null; an empty required field (kiln_type, cone, fired_at) means the whole row is skipped and counted — skipping is not an error and must not raise.
In the importer, keep every string byte-for-byte as it appears in the file: no trimming, no case folding, no deduplication.

Gas firing rows are now supported everywhere, import included, treated like electric — the former 'skip gas with a warning' importer rule was retired — with one exception: rows whose atmosphere column reads 'reduction' must get an oos flag set to true.
For `show`, print the atmosphere line only for gas batches; electric batches must never show it.
